turns.script: Okay so here's the thing, I've been working on this side project for a couple of months now, it's basically a little app that tracks what I eat and suggests recipes, and it was going great at first, but lately every time I add a feature something else breaks, and I'm starting to wonder if I should just rewrite the whole thing from scratch, or if that's a terrible idea and I should just add tests and clean it up bit by bit. What would you do?
turns.asr_text: Okay, so here's the thing. I've been working on this side project for a couple of months now. It's basically a little app that tracks what I eat and suggests recipes. And it was going great at first, but lately every time I add a feature, something else breaks. And I'm starting to wonder if I should just rewrite the whole thing from scratch, or if that's a terrible idea and I should just add tests and clean it up bit by bit. What would you do?

turns.text_generated:
Hey, that's a classic developer dilemma! Honestly, it really depends on the state of the codebase. If the foundation is super shaky—like, tons of spaghetti code that's hard to follow and fix—then a rewrite might make sense. But rewrites can be risky, and they can take way longer than you'd think.

On the other hand, if the core of your app is solid, you might just need to refactor in smaller, manageable chunks. Writing tests is a great idea no matter what—it gives you a safety net for future changes.

If I were in your shoes, I'd probably lean toward cleaning it up bit by bit—especially if you've already got a working product. That way, you can improve things incrementally, and you won’t lose all your momentum. But if you find yourself constantly wrestling with the old code and it’s slowing down your progress big time, then a rewrite might be worth it. It's all about balancing the time you put in now versus the time you'll save in the future.
